etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English bribe, from Old French briber (“go begging”), from the noun bribe (“a gift”).

definitions.definition: Something (usually money) given in exchange for influence or as an inducement to breaking the law.

quote.citation: c. 1613-1625, Henry Hobart, Yardly v. Ellill
quote.text: Undue reward for anything against justice is a bribe.

quote.citation: 2024 June 17, @InternetHippo, Twitter‎[1], archived from the original on 29 June 2024:
quote.text: The bribes I took did not influence me to become evil. I was evil from the beginning and the bribes were merely a bonus

quote.citation: 1744, Mark Akenside, The Pleasures of the Imagination:
quote.text: Not the bribes of sordid wealth can seduce to leave these everblooming sweets.
Remy, this was a bribe! Our whole marriage has been nothing but a series of bribes!

definitions.definition: (transitive) To give a bribe to; specifically, to ask a person to do something against their original will, in exchange for some type of reward or relief from potential trouble.

quote.citation: October 23, 1848, Frederick William Robertson, an address delivered at the Opening of The Working Men's Institute
quote.text: Neither is he worthy who bribes a man to vote against his conscience.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To gain by a bribe; to induce as by a bribe.
